newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria restarts reactor after minor failure.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria restarts reactor after minor failure.

text.p: Bulgaria on Tuesday started operations to put on stream its most modern Soviet-made reactor at Kozloduy, which was switched off last week due to a minor incident, a senior official said on Tuesday.
The executive director of the National Electricity Company Kozma Kuzmanov said tests had been finalised last night and the 1,000-megawatt reactor was being restarted.
"We expect to connect it to the national power grid tomorrow," Kuzmanov told Reuters.

Reactor number six was switched off on November 11 due to a failure of an air relief valve in its second steam generator, officials said, adding that no radioactive material was involved in the incident.
Experts assessed the incident as zero according to the International Nuclear Event Scale (INES).

Bulgaria lacks energy resources and relies on all six Kozloduy reactors to avoid a power crisis this winter. The 3,760-megawatt plant on the Danube river provides more than 40 percent of the country's power needs.
Kozloduy officials said five out of all six reactors were currently in operation with a total production of 1,810 megawatts.
The plant switched off its oldest 440-megawatt reactor in May amid international concern over the safety of its vessel's metal.

Energy officials said the first results of analysis of the metal's samples carried out by Russia's Korchatov Institute showed the metal was in good condition and could be put in operation this winter. Final results are expected in the middle of December.
Kuzmanov said experts from the Korchatov Institute had arrived in Sofia on Tuesday to discuss preliminary results with Bulgarian officials.
